aliases: Observation of the rare decay Bs0 -> mu+ mu- (CMS and LHCb combined)

claim.quote: The combined analysis produces the first observation of the $B^0_s\to\mu^+\mu^-$ decay, with a statistical significance exceeding six standard deviations, and the best measurement of its branching fraction so far.

date.note: arXiv preprint submitted 17 November 2014 (v1); published as Nature 522, 68-72 (4 June 2015).

name: Observation of the rare decay B⁰ₛ → μ⁺μ⁻ (CMS and LHCb combined)
notes: A joint CMS and LHCb result; only the CMS experiment and collaboration are linked on this record.

significance.quote: a statistical significance exceeding six standard deviations

summary.plain: CMS and LHCb combined their 2011–2012 data to make the first observation of a B_s meson decaying into two muons, a decay the Standard Model predicts to be very rare: about four in every billion B_s mesons produced.
summary.technical: Joint CMS+LHCb analysis of 7 TeV (2011) and 8 TeV (2012) data: first observation of B_s → μ⁺μ⁻ with a statistical significance exceeding six standard deviations, and evidence for B⁰ → μ⁺μ⁻ with a significance of three standard deviations; the branching fractions are statistically compatible with SM predictions.

title: Observation of the rare $B^0_s\to\mu^+\mu^-$ decay from the combined analysis of CMS and LHCb data
why_it_matters: The paper says a difference between the observed branching fractions and the Standard Model predictions would provide a direction in which the Standard Model should be extended; the abstract says the measurements are statistically compatible with SM predictions and impose stringent constraints on several theories beyond the SM.
